title: Medication vs. Therapy: How to Choose (Or Use Both)
description: Should you try medication, therapy, or both? How to make the decision, what research shows about combining treatments, and when each works best.

content.text: One of the first questions people face when seeking mental health treatment: should I try medication, therapy, or both? Here's how to think through the decision.
For moderate to severe depression, combination therapy (medication + psychotherapy) is more effective than either alone, with 73% response rate vs ~50% for monotherapy.
However, for mild depression, therapy alone often works well. And some conditions respond better to one than the other.

items: Severe symptoms interfering with functioning
Strong biological component (family history, distinct episodes)
When you need faster relief
Conditions like bipolar disorder or schizophrenia
When therapy alone hasn't worked
Limited access to quality therapy
Mild to moderate symptoms
Situational causes (grief, relationship issues, life transitions)
Wanting to learn lasting coping skills
Preference to avoid medication side effects
Pregnancy (some therapies safer than meds)
When there's a lot to process (trauma, identity)
Medication can reduce symptoms enough to engage in therapy
Therapy provides skills that last after medication stops
They target different mechanisms
Better relapse prevention than medication alone
How severe are my symptoms?
How much are they affecting my daily life?
Do I have the time and access for regular therapy?
How do I feel about taking medication?
Have I tried one approach that didn't work?
What does my provider recommend?

content.text: This isn't a permanent decision. You can start with one approach and add or switch later based on how you respond.

There's no universal right answer. For mild symptoms, either can work. For moderate to severe, combination therapy has the best evidence. The best treatment is one you'll actually follow through with. Discuss options with a mental health provider who can assess your specific situation.
